data.description: Ability to use, monitor, and troubleshoot automated data acquisition and assessment platforms, intervening effectively for exception cases.
data.historic work: Key Activities - 'Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs; develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary.'
data.change to work: The focus of project leadership will shift from manual tasks to oversight of automated workflows and intervention in complex exceptions. Project scope increasingly involves curating and validating results of automated acquisition, leading negotiation and resolution in non-routine circumstances, and addressing advanced legal/privacy or data sensitivity challenges.
data.justification: The update requires operational understanding of how data acquisition automation tools work and ability to identify when exception handling is needed.

data.description: Skill in establishing, negotiating, and sustaining non-traditional external data source partnerships, especially across multiple sectors.
data.historic work: Key Activities - 'Responsible for outreach and collaboration with a variety of stakeholders ... to establish relationships to leverage new methods and data sources, understand user needs and keep abreast of economic trends and developments, and providing expert advice and analysis.'
data.change to work: Automated tools handle the bulk of standard outreach and integration. The specialist's collaboration responsibilities evolve toward managing strategic relations with new data providers (e.g., tech firms, private sector data holders), and ensuring ongoing compliance and partnership innovation. Expertise will be needed in navigating and establishing partnerships involving emerging data assets.
data.justification: Shift from routine collaboration to advanced negotiation and management of strategic data partnerships requires new relationship-building and negotiation expertise.

data.development area: Advanced Negotiation Techniques for Data Acquisition
data.description: Mastery of negotiation strategies for complex, sensitive, or proprietary data, including terms related to privacy, usage, and access.
data.historic work: Key Activities - 'Participates in or leads data acquisition negotiations.'
data.change to work: Negotiations are now focused on edge/corner cases (novel, proprietary, or sensitive data), requiring advanced techniques beyond current-breadth negotiations. This elevates both the complexity and frequency of high-stakes negotiation scenarios.
data.justification: Negotiations increasingly require advanced, cross-disciplinary approaches for novel/sensitive data.

data.description: Ability to supervise, audit, and enhance automated integration/analytics solutions; diagnose/investigate anomalies in automated work outputs.
data.historic work: Key Activities - 'Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products.'
data.change to work: Specialist's management is focused on oversight and validation of outputs and processes generated by automation, rather than direct hands-on integration. More attention is given to ensuring quality, trustworthiness, and adequacy of automated outcomes, and to addressing edge-case integrations.
data.justification: Oversight responsibility means deeper technical understanding of automation and validation processes.

data.description: Ability to set up, monitor, and resolve issues with automated data acquisition and processing tools; identify when manual intervention is required.
data.historic work: Technical Activities
data.change to work: Technical activities pivot from manual data handling to configuring, evaluating, and improving automated systems. The specialist intervenes primarily when automated workflows encounter novel requirements or fail.
data.justification: Routine manual work is replaced by automation configuration and troubleshooting requirements.

data.description: Ability to navigate and apply enterprise data registry standards, ensuring variable definitions and metadata align with organizational requirements for interoperability and automation.
data.historic work: Key Activities: Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs; develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary.
data.change to work: This activity will increasingly require the Specialist to prioritize variable standards—ensuring that all data integration projects use variables compliant with enterprise registries and are ready for automated ingestion and reuse. Manual variable reconciliation will largely be replaced by registry-based stewardship and quality assurance.
data.justification: Modernizing variable integration requires understanding enterprise registries and their protocols, a skill not emphasized in current work-description.
